title: Tenant flood rapid remediation and reservation corrector
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Follow-up ticket for the capacity event on 2026-03-09 where a tenant-side surge combined with a memory-leaking model caused reservation imbalance, KV-cache pressure, and cascade evictions across a Dedicated GPU cluster. This ticket coordinates immediate remediation, medium-term fixes to the reservation autoscaler, and runbook + observability additions to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-09 at ~03:40 UTC several tenants experienced elevated tail latency and failed requests. Root cause analysis shows a simultaneous tenant flood plus a regression in the reservation allocator that allowed fractional reservations to drift >30% from observed usage. The noisy tenant exhausted GPU memory via a leaking inference loop which caused eviction storms and soft-reservation starvation for adjacent tenants. Autoscaler burst logic also allowed aggressive soft bursts without timely decay, amplifying oscillation.

2026-03-09 03:40 UTC - Automated eviction started, incident responders paged
2026-03-09 03:48 UTC - Emergency soft-quarantine applied to top noisy tenant (manual cgroup throttling)
2026-03-09 04:10 UTC - Temporary reservation correction deployed (hotfix: reserve floor enforcement)

2026-03-10 - Post-incident triage and data collection (telemetry, KV-cache stats, allocator logs)
root_cause: Combination of: (1) a memory leak in an inference loop for tenant A causing persistent GPU memory pressure; (2) recent allocator regression that allowed fractional reservation drift and didn't backfill quickly; (3) burst decay parameters too permissive causing prolonged soft bursts and interfering with reservation reconvergence.
decisions: Ship hotfix to enforce reservation floor and reject allocation requests that would drive node reservation drift >20%
Introduce ephemeral tenant fencing (soft-quarantine) when per-tenant memory share exceeds threshold for >30s
Rollback the allocator change from runtime-1.26 that loosened fractional accounting until autosculptor validations pass
Tune burst token decay to 50% faster half-life for Dedicated clusters by default and surface tunables in Console

validation_plan: Deploy hotfix to a single canary rack, validate no eviction regressions for 48h
Run synthetic tenant flood test (3 minute sustained high QPS) and verify soft-quarantine triggers within 45s
Replay 03-09 telemetry through autosculptor simulation and confirm reservation convergence within 5 minutes
Monitor per-tenant tail latency and eviction counts in the next two production deploy windows
rollback_plan: If hotfix causes allocation failures or incorrect rejections in canary, immediately revert to previous allocator configuration, disable reserve_floor enforcement for affected racks, and open an incident on #dedicated-capacity. Full rollback checklist is maintained in the emergency runbook.

We will not change default burst policies for Hosted customers in this rollout — only Dedicated clusters are affected.
This incident surfaced cross-team ownership gaps between Allocator, KV-cache, and Observability teams; add a short-term liaison pair for the next 4 weeks.
